**Alicia Christian** "**Jodie**" **Foster** (born November 19, 1962) is an American actress and filmmaker. Foster started her career as a [child actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Child_actor "Child actor") before establishing herself as a leading actress in film. As a performer, she is known for her versatility. She has received [several accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Jodie_Foster "List of awards and nominations received by Jodie Foster"), including two [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"), three [BAFTA Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Film_Awards "British Academy Film Awards"), four [Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards"), a [Primetime Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award "Primetime Emmy Award"), the [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award"), and the [Honorary Palme d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary_Palme_d'Or "Honorary Palme d'Or").

Foster began her career as a child model and gained recognition as a [teen idol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_idol "Teen idol") through [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney "Disney") films, including _[Napoleon and Samantha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon\_and\_Samantha "Napoleon and Samantha")_ (1972) and _[Freaky Friday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freaky\_Friday\_(1976\_film) "Freaky Friday (1976 film)")_ (1976). She appeared in [Martin Scorsese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Scorsese "Martin Scorsese")'s comedy-drama _[Alice Doesn't Live Here Anymore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice\_Doesn't\_Live\_Here\_Anymore "Alice Doesn't Live Here Anymore")_ (1974) and was nominated for an [Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress") for her role as a 12-year-old prostitute in his _[Taxi Driver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxi\_Driver "Taxi Driver")_ (1976).

Other early films include _[Tom Sawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom\_Sawyer\_(1973\_film) "Tom Sawyer (1973 film)")_ (1973) and _[Bugsy Malone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bugsy\_Malone "Bugsy Malone")_ (1976). After attending [Yale University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_University "Yale University"), Foster transitioned into mature leading roles and won two [Academy Awards for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actress "Academy Award for Best Actress") for playing a rape victim in _[The Accused](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Accused\_(1988\_film) "The Accused (1988 film)")_ (1988) and [Clarice Starling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clarice_Starling "Clarice Starling") in _[The Silence of the Lambs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Silence\_of\_the\_Lambs\_(film) "The Silence of the Lambs (film)")_ (1991). She has also been nominated for _[Nell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nell\_(film) "Nell (film)")_ (1994) and _[Nyad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyad\_(film) "Nyad (film)")_ (2023). On television, Foster starred in the [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") anthology series _[True Detective: Night Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True\_Detective\_(season\_4) "True Detective (season 4)")_ (2024), for which she won a [Primetime Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Lead_Actress_in_a_Limited_or_Anthology_Series_or_Movie "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie") and [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_%E2%80%93_Miniseries_or_Television_Film "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress – Miniseries or Television Film").

Foster has directed four feature length films: _[Little Man Tate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little\_Man\_Tate "Little Man Tate")_ (1991), _[Home for the Holidays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home\_for\_the\_Holidays\_(1995\_film) "Home for the Holidays (1995 film)")_ (1995), _[The Beaver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Beaver\_(film) "The Beaver (film)")_ (2011), and _[Money Monster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Money\_Monster "Money Monster")_ (2016).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-2) She founded a production company, Egg Pictures, in 1992. Foster also received Primetime Emmy nominations for [producing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Television_Movie "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Television Movie")_[The Baby Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Baby\_Dance "The Baby Dance")_ (1998) and for [directing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Directing_for_a_Comedy_Series "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Directing for a Comedy Series") the _[Orange Is the New Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orange\_Is\_the\_New\_Black "Orange Is the New Black")_ episode "[Lesbian Request Denied](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesbian_Request_Denied "Lesbian Request Denied")" (2013). She has also directed episodes of _[Tales from the Darkside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tales\_from\_the\_Darkside "Tales from the Darkside")_ (1988), _[House of Cards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House\_of\_Cards\_(American\_TV\_series) "House of Cards (American TV series)")_ (2014), the _[Black Mirror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Mirror "Black Mirror")_ episode "[Arkangel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkangel_(Black_Mirror) "Arkangel (Black Mirror)")" (2017), and _[Tales from the Loop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tales\_from\_the\_Loop "Tales from the Loop")_ (2020).

## Early life and education

Alicia Christian Foster[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-scotsman-4) was born on November 19, 1962, in Los Angeles, California, the youngest child of Evelyn Ella "Brandy" (née Almond; 1928–2019)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-5) and Lucius Fisher Foster III (1922–2016), a businessman.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013182%E2%80%93183-6) She is of German,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-rollingstone-7) Irish, and English heritage.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-8) On her father's side, she is descended from [John Alden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Alden "John Alden"), who arrived in North America on the _[Mayflower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayflower "Mayflower")_ in 1620.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013182%E2%80%93183-6)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-BrandyFoster1976-9)

Her parents' marriage ended before she was born, and she never established a relationship with her father.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013182%E2%80%93183-6)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-NYT_1991-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-60Minutes-11) She has three older full siblings: Lucinda, Constance "Connie", and [Lucius "Buddy"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddy_Foster "Buddy Foster"); as well as three half-brothers from her father's earlier marriage.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-BrandyFoster1976-9) Following the divorce, Brandy raised the children with her female partner in Los Angeles.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013182%E2%80%93183-6)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-observer-12) She worked as a publicist for film producer [Arthur P. Jacobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_P._Jacobs "Arthur P. Jacobs") until focusing on managing the acting careers of Buddy and Jodie.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013182%E2%80%93183-6)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-BrandyFoster1976-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-NYT_1991-10) Although Foster was officially named Alicia, her siblings began calling her "Jodie", and the name stuck.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-scotsman-4)

Foster was a [gifted child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Child_prodigy "Child prodigy") who learned to read at age three.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013182%E2%80%93183-6)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-NYT_1991-10) She attended the [Lycée Français de Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyc%C3%A9e_Fran%C3%A7ais_de_Los_Angeles "Lycée Français de Los Angeles"), a French-language [prep school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University-preparatory_school "University-preparatory school").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-NYT_1991-10) Her fluency in French has enabled her to act in French films. She also [dubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubbing_(filmmaking) "Dubbing (filmmaking)") herself in French-language versions of most of her English-language films.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013182%E2%80%93183-6)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-13) At her graduation in 1980, she delivered the [valedictorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valedictorian "Valedictorian") address for the school's French division.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-NYT_1991-10)

She subsequently studied at [Yale University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_University "Yale University"),[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-60Minutes-11)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Ebertcollege-14) where she majored in [African-American literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_literature "African-American literature"). She wrote her thesis on [Toni Morrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toni_Morrison "Toni Morrison") under the guidance of [Henry Louis Gates Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Louis_Gates_Jr. "Henry Louis Gates Jr.") and graduated _[magna cum laude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magna\_cum\_laude "Magna cum laude")_ in 1985.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013182%E2%80%93183-6)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-seniorthesis-17) She returned to Yale in 1993 to address the graduating class and received an honorary [Doctor of Fine Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_of_Fine_Arts "Doctor of Fine Arts") degree in 1997.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-yale.edu-19) In 2018, she was awarded the Yale Undergraduate Lifetime Achievement Award.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-20)

## Career

### Career beginnings

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/Paper_Moon_TV_series_Foster_Connelly_1974.jpg/250px-Paper_Moon_TV_series_Foster_Connelly_1974.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Paper_Moon_TV_series_Foster_Connelly_1974.jpg)

Foster with [Christopher Connelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Connelly "Christopher Connelly") in a publicity photo for _[Paper Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paper\_Moon\_(American\_TV\_series) "Paper Moon (American TV series)")_ (1974), one of her first starring roles

Foster's career began with an appearance in a [Coppertone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coppertone_(sunscreen) "Coppertone (sunscreen)") television advertisement in 1965, when she was three years old.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-NYT_1991-10)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Sonneborn-2002-21)(p 73)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013183%E2%80%93184-22) Her mother had intended only for Jodie's older brother Buddy to audition, but had taken Jodie with them to the casting call, where she was noticed by the casting agents.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-BrandyFoster1976-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-NYT_1991-10)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Sonneborn-2002-21)(p 73) The television spot led to more advertising work and in 1968 to a minor appearance in the sitcom _[Mayberry R.F.D.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayberry\_R.F.D. "Mayberry R.F.D.")_, in which her brother starred.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-NYT_1991-10)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Sonneborn-2002-21)(p 74) In the following years, Foster continued working in advertising and appeared in over 50 television shows, including _[Gunsmoke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunsmoke "Gunsmoke")_, _[The Doris Day Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Doris\_Day\_Show "The Doris Day Show")_, _[My Three Sons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Three\_Sons "My Three Sons")_, _[Bonanza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonanza "Bonanza")_, and _[Kung Fu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kung\_Fu\_(1972\_TV\_series) "Kung Fu (1972 TV series)")_; she and her brother became the breadwinners of the family during this time.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-BrandyFoster1976-9)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Sonneborn-2002-21)(p 73) She had recurring roles in _[The Courtship of Eddie's Father](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Courtship\_of\_Eddie's\_Father\_(TV\_series) "The Courtship of Eddie's Father (TV series)")_ (1969–1971) and _[Bob & Carol & Ted & Alice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob\_&\_Carol\_&\_Ted\_&\_Alice\_(TV\_series) "Bob & Carol & Ted & Alice (TV series)")_ (1973), voiced [Pugsley Addams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pugsley_Addams "Pugsley Addams") in [The _Addams Family_ animated series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Addams_Family_(1973_TV_series) "The Addams Family (1973 TV series)") (1973–1975), and starred opposite [Christopher Connelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Connelly_(actor) "Christopher Connelly (actor)") in the short-lived _[Paper Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paper\_Moon\_(American\_TV\_series) "Paper Moon (American TV series)")_ (1974), adapted from [the hit film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paper_Moon_(film) "Paper Moon (film)").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Sonneborn-2002-21)(p 73)

Foster also appeared in films, mostly for [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Pictures "Walt Disney Pictures").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Sonneborn-2002-21)(p 73) After a role in the television film _Menace on the Mountain_ (1970), she made her feature film debut in _[Napoleon and Samantha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon\_and\_Samantha "Napoleon and Samantha")_ (1972), playing a girl who befriends a boy, played by [Johnny Whitaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Whitaker "Johnny Whitaker"), and his pet lion. She was accidentally grabbed by the lion on set, which left her with scars on her back.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-warhol-23) Her other early film work includes the [Raquel Welch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raquel_Welch "Raquel Welch") vehicle _[Kansas City Bomber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas\_City\_Bomber "Kansas City Bomber")_ (1972), the [Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_(genre) "Western (genre)")_[One Little Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One\_Little\_Indian\_(film) "One Little Indian (film)")_ (1973), the [Mark Twain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Twain "Mark Twain") adaptation _[Tom Sawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom\_Sawyer\_(1973\_film) "Tom Sawyer (1973 film)")_ (1973), and [Martin Scorsese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Scorsese "Martin Scorsese")'s _[Alice Doesn't Live Here Anymore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice\_Doesn't\_Live\_Here\_Anymore "Alice Doesn't Live Here Anymore")_ (1974), in which she appeared in a supporting role as a "[Ripple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavored_fortified_wines "Flavored fortified wines")-drinking street kid".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-NYT_1991-10)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Sonneborn-2002-21)(p 73)

Foster said she loved acting as a child and values her early work for the experience it gave her: "Some people get quick breaks and declare, 'I'll never do commercials! That's so lowbrow!' I want to tell them, 'Well, I'm real glad you've got a pretty face, because I worked for 20 years doing that stuff and I feel it's really invaluable; it really taught me a lot.'"[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-postcollege-24)

### 1970s: _Taxi Driver_ and teenage stardom

Foster's mother was concerned that her daughter's career would end by the time she grew out of playing children and decided that Foster should also begin acting in films for adult audiences.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollinger2006141-25) After the minor supporting role in _Alice_, Scorsese cast her in the role of a child prostitute in _[Taxi Driver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxi\_Driver "Taxi Driver")_ (1976).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013184%E2%80%93185-26) To be able to do the film, Foster had to undergo psychiatric assessment and was accompanied by a social worker on set.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-afitaxi-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTERausch201030%E2%80%9331-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013185-29) Her older sister Connie acted as her [stand-in](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stand-in "Stand-in") in sexually suggestive scenes.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTERausch201030%E2%80%9331-28)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-30) Foster later commented on the role, saying that she hated "the idea that everybody thinks if a kid's going to be an actress it means that she has to play [Shirley Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shirley_Temple "Shirley Temple") or someone's little sister."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-31) During the filming, Foster developed a bond with co-star [Robert De Niro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_De_Niro "Robert De Niro"), who saw "serious potential" in her and dedicated time to rehearsing scenes with her.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTERausch201034-32)

Foster called _Taxi Driver_ a life-changing experience and said it was "the first time anyone asked me to create a character that wasn't myself. It was the first time I realized that acting wasn't this hobby you just sort of did, but that there was actually some craft."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-NYT_1991-10)_Taxi Driver_ won the [Palme d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palme_d'Or "Palme d'Or") at the [Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_Cannes_Film_Festival "1976 Cannes Film Festival"), where Foster impressed journalists when she acted as a French interpreter at the press conference.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-afitaxi-27)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-33)_Taxi Driver_ was a critical and commercial success, and earned her a supporting actress [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award") nomination, as well as two [BAFTAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA "BAFTA"), a [David di Donatello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_di_Donatello "David di Donatello") and a [National Society of Film Critics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Society_of_Film_Critics_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "National Society of Film Critics Award for Best Supporting Actress") award.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-NYT_1991-10)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-afitaxi-27) The film is considered one of the best in history by the [American Film Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Film_Institute "American Film Institute")[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-afitaxi-27) and _[Sight & Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sight\_&\_Sound "Sight & Sound")_,[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-bfi-34) and has been preserved in the [National Film Registry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Registry "National Film Registry").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-loc.gov-35)

Foster also acted in another film nominated for the Palme d'Or in 1976, _[Bugsy Malone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bugsy\_Malone "Bugsy Malone")_,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Brickman-36) a British [musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_film "Musical film") that parodied films about [Prohibition Era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prohibition_Era "Prohibition Era") gangsters by having all roles played by children. Foster appeared in a major supporting role as a star of a [speakeasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speakeasy "Speakeasy") show.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-37) Director [Alan Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Parker "Alan Parker") was impressed by her, saying that "she takes such an intelligent interest in the way the film is being made that if I had been run over by a bus I think she was probably the only person on the set able to take over as director."[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollinger2006155-38) She gained several positive notices for her performance, with [Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") of the _[Chicago Sun-Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_Sun-Times "Chicago Sun-Times")_ writing: "at thirteen she was already getting the roles that grown-up actresses complained weren't being written for women anymore".[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-39)_[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_ called her "outstanding",[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-40) and [Vincent Canby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincent_Canby "Vincent Canby") of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ called her "the star of the show".[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-41) Foster's two BAFTAs were awarded jointly for her performances in _Taxi Driver_ and _Bugsy Malone_.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-42)

Her third film release in 1976 was the independent drama _[Echoes of a Summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Echoes\_of\_a\_Summer "Echoes of a Summer")_, which had been filmed two years earlier.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-echoes-43)_The New York Times_ named Foster's performance as a terminally ill girl the film's "main strength"[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-echoes-43) and [Gene Siskel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_Siskel "Gene Siskel") of the _[Chicago Tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_Tribune "Chicago Tribune")_ wrote that she "is not a good child actress; she's just a good actress", although both reviewers panned the film.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-44) Foster's fourth film of 1976 was the Canadian-French thriller _[The Little Girl Who Lives Down the Lane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Little\_Girl\_Who\_Lives\_Down\_the\_Lane "The Little Girl Who Lives Down the Lane")_, in which she starred opposite [Martin Sheen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Sheen "Martin Sheen").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEErb201096-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013188%E2%80%93189-46) The film combined aspects of thriller and horror genres, and showed Foster as a mysterious young girl living on her own in a small town. The performance earned her a [Saturn Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturn_Award_for_Best_Actress "Saturn Award for Best Actress").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013188-47) In November, Foster hosted _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday\_Night\_Live "Saturday Night Live")_, becoming the youngest person to do so until [Drew Barrymore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drew_Barrymore "Drew Barrymore") hosted at age 7 in 1982.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-warhol-23) Her final film of the year was the Disney comedy _[Freaky Friday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freaky\_Friday\_(1976\_film) "Freaky Friday (1976 film)")_, "her first true star vehicle".[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013188-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEErb201087-48)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Brickman-36) She played a tomboy teen who accidentally changes bodies with her mother, and she later said the film marked a "transitional period" when she began to grow out of child roles.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEErb201087-48) It received mainly positive reviews,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEErb201086-49) and was a box-office success,[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-50) gaining Foster a [Golden Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_%E2%80%93_Motion_Picture_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress – Motion Picture Musical or Comedy") nomination for her performance.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-51)

As Foster grew, her mother wanted photos to reflect Foster's ability to take on adult roles, so she arranged for [Emilio Lari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilio_Lari "Emilio Lari") to do a partially nude photoshoot. The photoshoot was taken at a rented estate in Los Angeles, with Foster's mother and Lari's wife on set. Estimates of the year of the photoshoot range between 1975 and 1979, when Foster was between 13 and 16.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-54) After her breakthrough year, Foster spent nine months living in France, where she starred in _[Moi, fleur bleue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moi,\_fleur\_bleue "Moi, fleur bleue")_ (1977) and recorded several songs for its soundtrack.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Ebertcollege-14)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTESnodgrass2008285-55) Her other films released in 1977 were the Italian comedy _[Casotto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beach\_House\_(1977\_film) "Beach House (1977 film)")_ and the Disney [heist film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heist_film "Heist film")_[Candleshoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candleshoe "Candleshoe")_, which was filmed in England and co-starred [David Niven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Niven "David Niven") and [Helen Hayes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Hayes "Helen Hayes").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013188-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEErb201087-48)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Thomson-56) After its release, Foster did not appear in any new releases until 1980, the year she turned 18.

### 1980s: Transition to adult roles and _The Accused_

In 1980, she gained positive notices for her performances in the independent films _[Foxes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foxes\_(film) "Foxes (film)")_ and _[Carny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carny\_(1980\_film) "Carny (1980 film)")_ (1980),[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-57)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Sonneborn-2002-21)(p 73–74)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013189-58) before becoming a full-time student at Yale in 1981.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Sonneborn-2002-21)(p 73–74)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-actors-59) She later said that going to college changed her thoughts about acting, which she had previously thought was an unintelligent profession. She realized that "what I really wanted to do was to act and there was nothing stupid about it."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-postcollege-24)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-actors-59)

Although Foster prioritized college during these years, she continued making films on her summer vacations.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Ebertcollege-14) These were _[O'Hara's Wife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O'Hara's\_Wife "O'Hara's Wife")_ (1982), the television film _Svengali_ (1983), the [John Irving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Irving "John Irving") adaptation _[The Hotel New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hotel\_New\_Hampshire\_(film) "The Hotel New Hampshire (film)")_ (1984), _[The Blood of Others](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blood\_of\_Others\_(film) "The Blood of Others (film)")_ (1984), and the period drama _[Mesmerized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Letter\_to\_George "My Letter to George")_ (1986), which she also co-produced.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013192-60) None of them gained large audiences or critical appreciation.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollinger2006143-61)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Sonneborn-2002-21)(p 73–74)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/Jodie_Foster_%281989%29.jpg/250px-Jodie_Foster_%281989%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jodie_Foster_(1989).jpg)

Foster at the Governor's Ball after winning an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actress "Academy Award for Best Actress") for _[The Accused](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Accused\_(1988\_film) "The Accused (1988 film)")_ (1988). Her performance as a rape survivor marked her breakthrough into adult roles.

After graduating from Yale in 1985, Foster struggled to find further acting work. In 1987, her first film after college, the neo-[noir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_noir "Film noir")_[Siesta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siesta\_(film) "Siesta (film)")_ (1987), was rated a failure,[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013194-62)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-63) but her next project, the independent film _[Five Corners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five\_Corners\_(film) "Five Corners (film)")_ (1987), was better received. A moderate critical success, it earned Foster an [Independent Spirit Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_Spirit_Awards "Independent Spirit Awards") for her performance as a woman whose sexual assaulter returns to stalk her.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013193-64)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Sonneborn-2002-21)(p 73–74)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-65)

The following year, Foster made her debut as a director with the episode "Do Not Open This Box" for the horror anthology series _[Tales from the Darkside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tales\_from\_the\_Darkside "Tales from the Darkside")_,[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-66) and starred in the romantic drama _[Stealing Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stealing\_Home "Stealing Home")_ (1988) opposite [Mark Harmon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Harmon "Mark Harmon"). The film was a critical and commercial failure,[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-67) with Roger Ebert "wondering if any movie could possibly be that bad".[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-68)

Foster's breakthrough into adult roles came with her performance as a rape survivor in _[The Accused](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Accused\_(1988\_film) "The Accused (1988 film)")_ (1988).[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013194-62)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollinger2006143-61)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Sonneborn-2002-21)(p 73–74) Based on the real criminal case involving [Cheryl Araujo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheryl_Araujo "Cheryl Araujo"), the film focuses on the aftermath of a [gang rape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gang_rape "Gang rape") and its survivor's fight for justice in the face of [victim blaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victim_blaming "Victim blaming"). Before making it, Foster was having doubts about whether to continue her career and planned to start graduate studies, but decided to give acting "one last try" in _The Accused_.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-actors-59) She had to audition twice for the role and was cast only after several more established actors turned it down, as the film's producers were wary of her due to her previous failures and because she was still remembered as a "chubby teenager".[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-actors-59)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Sonneborn-2002-21)(p 74)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollinger201245-69)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen2013194-62) Due to the subject matter, the filming was a difficult experience for the cast and crew, especially the shooting of the rape scene, which took five days.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-NYT_1991-10) Foster was unhappy with her performance and feared that it would end her career.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollinger201246-70) Instead, _The Accused_ received positive reviews, with Foster's performance receiving widespread acclaim[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollinger201245-69) and earning her [Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actress "Academy Award for Best Actress"), [Golden Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_-_Motion_Picture_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress - Motion Picture Drama") and [National Board of Review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Board_of_Review_Award_for_Best_Actress "National Board of Review Award for Best Actress") awards, as well as a nomination for a [BAFTA Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Leading_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actress in a Leading Role").

### 1990s: Box-office success, directorial debut and Egg Pictures

Foster's first film release after the success of _The Accused_ was the thriller _[The Silence of the Lambs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Silence\_of\_the\_Lambs\_(film) "The Silence of the Lambs (film)")_ (1991). She portrayed [FBI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation "Federal Bureau of Investigation") trainee [Clarice Starling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clarice_Starling "Clarice Starling"), who is sent to interview incarcerated serial killer [Hannibal Lecter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannibal_Lecter "Hannibal Lecter") ([Anthony Hopkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Hopkins "Anthony Hopkins")) in order to hunt another serial killer, [Jame "Buffalo Bill" Gumb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Bill_(character) "Buffalo Bill (character)") ([Ted Levine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Levine "Ted Levine")). Foster later named the role one of her favorites.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollinger201246-70) She had read [the novel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silence_of_the_Lambs_(novel) "Silence of the Lambs (novel)") it was based on after its publication in 1988 and had attempted to purchase its film rights,[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-71) as it featured "a real female heroine" and its plot was not "about steroids and brawn, [but] about using your mind and using your insufficiencies to combat the villain."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-NYT_1991-10) Despite her enthusiasm, director [Jonathan Demme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Demme "Jonathan Demme") did not initially want to cast her, but the producers overruled him.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-demmenme-72) Demme's view of Foster changed during the production, and he later credited her for helping him define the character.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-demmenme-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-73)

Released in February 1991, _The Silence of the Lambs_ became one of the biggest hits of the year, grossing close to $273 million,[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-74)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-75) with a positive critical reception. Foster received largely positive reviews[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollinger201246-70) and won Academy, Golden Globe, and BAFTA awards for her portrayal of Starling; _Silence_ won five Academy Awards overall,[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-76) becoming one of the few films to win in all main categories. In contrast, some reviewers criticized the film as misogynist for its focus on brutal murders of women, and [homo-](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homophobia "Homophobia")/[transphobic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transphobic "Transphobic") due to its portrayal of "Buffalo Bill" as [bisexual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bisexual "Bisexual") and [transgender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender "Transgender"). Much of the criticism was directed at Foster, who the critics claimed was herself a lesbian.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollinger201246%E2%80%9347-77) Despite the controversy, the film is considered a modern classic: Starling and Lecter are included on the American Film Institute's top ten of [the greatest film heroes and villains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFI's_100_Years...100_Heroes_&_Villains "AFI's 100 Years...100 Heroes & Villains"), and the film is preserved in the National Film Registry.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-loc.gov-35) Later in 1991, Foster also starred in the unsuccessful low-budget thriller _[Catchfire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catchfire "Catchfire")_, which had been filmed before _Silence_, but was released after it in an attempt to profit from its success.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-78)

In October 1991, Foster released her first feature film as a director, _[Little Man Tate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little\_Man\_Tate "Little Man Tate")_, a drama about a child prodigy who struggles to come to terms with being different.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-79) The main role was played by previously unknown actor [Adam Hann-Byrd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Hann-Byrd "Adam Hann-Byrd"), and Foster co-starred as his working-class single mother. She had found the script in the "[slush pile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slush_pile "Slush pile")" at [Orion Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orion_Pictures "Orion Pictures"),[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollinger201249-80) and explained that for her debut film she "wanted a piece that was not autobiographical, but that had to do with the 10 philosophies I've accumulated in the past 25 years. Every single one of them, if they weren't in the script from the beginning, they're there now."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-NYT_1991-10) Some reviewers felt that the film did not live up to the high expectations, and regarded it as "less adventurous than many films in which [she] had starred",[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollinger201249%E2%80%9351-81)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Thomson-56) but others praised it, like Roger Ebert, who called it "the kind of film you enjoy watching".[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-82) Regardless, it was a moderate box office success.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-83) Foster's final film appearance of the year came in a small role as a sex worker in _[Shadows and Fog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shadows\_and\_Fog "Shadows and Fog")_ (1991), directed by [Woody Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woody_Allen "Woody Allen"), with whom she had wanted to collaborate since the 1970s.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Ebertcollege-14)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/Jodie_Foster_1995.jpg/250px-Jodie_Foster_1995.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jodie_Foster_1995.jpg)

Foster working on _[Home for the Holidays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home\_for\_the\_Holidays\_(1995\_film) "Home for the Holidays (1995 film)")_, 1995

The nineties and onwards has seen Foster in more action-oriented roles. Foster starred in the period film _[Sommersby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sommersby "Sommersby")_ (1993), portraying a woman who begins to suspect that her husband ([Richard Gere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Gere "Richard Gere")) who returns home from the [Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War "American Civil War") is an impostor. She then replaced [Meg Ryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meg_Ryan "Meg Ryan") in the Western comedy _[Maverick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maverick\_(film) "Maverick (film)")_ (1994), playing a [con artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Con_artist "Con artist") opposite [Mel Gibson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mel_Gibson "Mel Gibson") and [James Garner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Garner "James Garner").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-84) She appeared in the sci-fi film _[Contact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contact\_(1997\_American\_film) "Contact (1997 American film)")_ (1997), and the commercially successful _[Panic Room](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panic\_Room "Panic Room")_ (2002). Other action films have included _[Flightplan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan "Flightplan")_ (2005) and _[Nim's Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nim's\_Island "Nim's Island")_ (2008). _[Elysium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elysium\_(film) "Elysium (film)")_ (2013) saw her opposite [Matt Damon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Damon "Matt Damon") in a dystopian thriller.

According to film scholar Karen Hollinger, these later films were more "conventionally feminine" roles.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollinger201251-85) Both _Sommersby_ and _Maverick_ were box office successes.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-86)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-87)

Foster had founded her own production company, Egg Pictures, a subsidiary of [PolyGram Filmed Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PolyGram_Filmed_Entertainment "PolyGram Filmed Entertainment") in 1992, and released its first production, _[Nell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nell\_(film) "Nell (film)")_, in December 1994.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollinger201253-88)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Sonneborn-2002-21)(p 74)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-89) It was directed by [Michael Apted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Apted "Michael Apted")and starred Foster in the titular role as a woman who grew up isolated in the [Appalachian Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appalachian_Mountains "Appalachian Mountains") and speaks her own invented language.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-nynell-90) The film was based on [Mark Handley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Handley "Mark Handley")'s play _[Idioglossia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idioglossia\_(play) "Idioglossia (play)")_, which interested Foster for its theme of "otherness", and because she "loved this idea of a woman who defies categorization, a creature who is labeled and categorized by people based on their own problems and their own prejudices and what they bring to the table."[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-nynell-90)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-91) Despite mixed reviews, it was a commercial success,[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-92)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollinger201254-93) and earned Foster a [Screen Actors Guild Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award "Screen Actors Guild Award") and nominations for an Academy Award and a Golden Globe for her acting performance.

The second film that Foster directed and produced for Egg Pictures was _[Home for the Holidays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home\_for\_the\_Holidays\_(1995\_film) "Home for the Holidays (1995 film)")_, released in late 1995. A [black comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_comedy "Black comedy") "set around a nightmarish [Thanksgiving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thanksgiving "Thanksgiving")", it starred [Holly Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holly_Hunter "Holly Hunter") and [Robert Downey Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Downey_Jr. "Robert Downey Jr.")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-scotsman-4)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-94) The film received a mixed critical response and was a commercial failure.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollinger2006162-95)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Sonneborn-2002-21)(p 74) In 1996, Foster received two honorary awards: the [Crystal Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women_in_Film_Crystal_+_Lucy_Awards#THE_CRYSTAL_AWARD "Women in Film Crystal + Lucy Awards"), awarded annually for women in the entertainment industry,[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-96) and the Berlinale Camera at the [46th Berlin International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/46th_Berlin_International_Film_Festival "46th Berlin International Film Festival").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Berlinale1996-97) She voiced a character in an episode of _[Frasier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frasier "Frasier")_ in 1996 and in an episode of _[The X-Files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_X-Files "The X-Files")_ in early 1997.

After _Nell_ (1994), Foster appeared in no new film releases until _[Contact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contact\_(1997\_American\_film) "Contact (1997 American film)")_ (1997), a science fiction film based on a novel by [Carl Sagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Sagan "Carl Sagan") and directed by [Robert Zemeckis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Zemeckis "Robert Zemeckis"). She starred as a scientist searching for extraterrestrial life in the [SETI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SETI "SETI") project.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-98) The film was a commercial success[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-99) and earned Foster a Saturn Award and a nomination for a Golden Globe.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-103) Foster next produced [Jane Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane_Anderson "Jane Anderson")'s television film _The Baby Dance_ (1998) for [Showtime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Showtime_(TV_network) "Showtime (TV network)").[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-babydance-104)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-105) Its story deals with a wealthy California couple who struggles with infertility and decides to adopt from a poor family in [Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana "Louisiana").[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-babydance-104) On her decision to produce for television, Foster stated that it was easier to take financial risks in that medium than in feature films.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-babydance-104) In 1998, she also moved her production company from PolyGram to [Paramount Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures").[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollinger201253-88) Also in 1998, asteroid [17744 Jodiefoster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/17744_Jodiefoster "17744 Jodiefoster") was named in her honor.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTESnodgrass2008287-106)

Foster's last film of the 1990s was the period drama _[Anna and the King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna\_and\_the\_King "Anna and the King")_ (1999), in which she starred opposite [Chow Yun-Fat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chow_Yun-Fat "Chow Yun-Fat"). It was based on [a fictionalized biography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_and_the_King_of_Siam_(novel) "Anna and the King of Siam (novel)") of British teacher [Anna Leonowens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_Leonowens "Anna Leonowens"), who taught the children of King [Mongkut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongkut "Mongkut") of [Siam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siam "Siam"), and whose story became well known as the musical _[The King and I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_King\_and\_I "The King and I")_. Foster was paid $15 million to portray Leonowens, making her one of the highest-paid female actors in Hollywood.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Sonneborn-2002-21)(p 74) The film was subject to controversy when the Thai government deemed it historically inaccurate and insulting to the royal family and banned its distribution in the country.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-107) It was a moderate commercial success,[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-108) but received mixed to negative reviews.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-109)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-110) Ebert panned the film, saying the role required Foster "to play beneath [her] intelligence"[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-111) and _The New York Times_ called it a "misstep" for her and accused her of only being "interested ... in sanctifying herself as an old-fashioned heroine than in taking on dramatically risky roles".[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-112)

### 2000s: Career setbacks and resurgence in thrillers

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/Jodie_Foster.4785.jpg/250px-Jodie_Foster.4785.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jodie_Foster.4785.jpg)

Foster at the premiere of [_The Brave One_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brave_One_(2007_film) "The Brave One (2007 film)") in 2007

Foster's first project of the new decade was [Keith Gordon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Gordon "Keith Gordon")'s film _[Waking the Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waking\_the\_Dead\_(film) "Waking the Dead (film)")_ (2000), which she produced.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-113) She declined to reprise her role as Clarice Starling in _[Hannibal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannibal\_(2001\_film) "Hannibal (2001 film)")_ (2001), with the part going instead to [Julianne Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julianne_Moore "Julianne Moore"), and concentrated on a new directorial project, _Flora Plum_.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-114) It was to focus on a 1930s circus and star [Claire Danes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claire_Danes "Claire Danes") and [Russell Crowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_Crowe "Russell Crowe"), but had to be shelved after Crowe was injured on set and could not complete filming on schedule; Foster unsuccessfully attempted to revive the project several times in the following years.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-scotsman-4)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-115)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-116) Controversially, she also expressed interest in directing and starring in a biographical film of [Nazi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi "Nazi") film director [Leni Riefenstahl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leni_Riefenstahl "Leni Riefenstahl"), who did not like the idea.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-117)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-118) In addition to these setbacks, Foster shut down Egg Pictures in 2001, saying that producing was "just a really thankless, bad job".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-scotsman-4)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollinger201253-88) The company's last production, _[The Dangerous Lives of Altar Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dangerous\_Lives\_of\_Altar\_Boys "The Dangerous Lives of Altar Boys")_, premiered at the [Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundance_Film_Festival "Sundance Film Festival") in January 2002. It received good reviews,[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollinger2006162-95) and had a limited theatrical release in the summer.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-119) After the cancellation of _Flora Plum_, Foster took on the main role in David Fincher's thriller _[Panic Room](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panic\_Room "Panic Room")_ after its intended star, [Nicole Kidman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicole_Kidman "Nicole Kidman"), had to drop out due to an injury on the set of _[Moulin Rouge!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moulin\_Rouge! "Moulin Rouge!")_.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-120) Before filming resumed, Foster was given only a week to prepare for the role of a woman who hides in a [panic room](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safe_room "Safe room") with her daughter when burglars invade their home.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-121) It grossed over $30 million on its North American opening weekend in March 2002, becoming the most successful film opening of Foster's career as of 2015[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jodie_Foster&action=edit).[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-122)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-123) In addition to being a box office success, the film also received largely positive reviews.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-124)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-125)

After a minor appearance in the French period drama _[A Very Long Engagement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Very\_Long\_Engagement "A Very Long Engagement")_ (2004), Foster starred in three more thrillers. The first was _[Flightplan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flightplan "Flightplan")_ (2005), in which she played a woman whose daughter vanishes during an overnight flight. It became a global box office success,[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-126) but received mixed reviews.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-127)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-128) It was followed by [Spike Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spike_Lee "Spike Lee")'s critically and commercially successful _[Inside Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inside\_Man "Inside Man")_ (2006), about a bank heist on [Wall Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall_Street "Wall Street"), which co-starred [Denzel Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denzel_Washington "Denzel Washington") and [Clive Owen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clive_Owen "Clive Owen").[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-129)[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-130) The third thriller, _[The Brave One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Brave\_One\_(2007\_film) "The Brave One (2007 film)")_ (2007), prompted some comparisons to _Taxi Driver_, as Foster played a New Yorker who becomes a vigilante after her fiancé is murdered.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-131) It was not a success,[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-132)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-133)[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-134) but earned Foster her sixth Golden Globe nomination. Her last film role of the decade was in the children's adventure film _[Nim's Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nim's\_Island "Nim's Island")_ (2008), in which she portrayed an [agoraphobic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agoraphobia "Agoraphobia") writer opposite [Gerard Butler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerard_Butler "Gerard Butler") and [Abigail Breslin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abigail_Breslin "Abigail Breslin"). It was the first comedy in which she had starred since _Maverick_ (1994), and was a commercial success but a critical failure.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-135)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-136) In 2009, she provided the voice for [Maggie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maggie_Simpson "Maggie Simpson") in a [tetralogy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetralogy "Tetralogy") episode of _[The Simpsons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Simpsons "The Simpsons")_ titled "[Four Great Women and a Manicure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_Great_Women_and_a_Manicure "Four Great Women and a Manicure")".[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Foster-137)

### 2010s: Focus on directing

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/Mel_Gibson_Jodie_Foster_Cannes_2011.jpg/250px-Mel_Gibson_Jodie_Foster_Cannes_2011.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mel_Gibson_Jodie_Foster_Cannes_2011.jpg)

Foster with co-star [Mel Gibson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mel_Gibson "Mel Gibson") at the premiere of _[The Beaver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Beaver\_(film) "The Beaver (film)")_ at the [2011 Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Cannes_Film_Festival "2011 Cannes Film Festival")

In the 2010s, Foster focused on directing and took fewer acting roles.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-indiew-138) In February 2011, she hosted the [36th César Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/36th_C%C3%A9sar_Awards "36th César Awards") in France, and the next month released her third feature film direction, _[The Beaver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Beaver\_(film) "The Beaver (film)")_ (2011), about a depressed man who develops an alternative personality based on a beaver hand puppet.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-139) It starred _Maverick_ co-star Mel Gibson and featured herself, [Anton Yelchin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anton_Yelchin "Anton Yelchin") and [Jennifer Lawrence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Lawrence "Jennifer Lawrence") in supporting roles as his family.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-140) Foster called its production "probably the biggest struggle of my professional career", partly due to the film's heavy subject matter but also due to the controversy that Gibson generated when he was accused of [domestic violence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domestic_violence "Domestic violence") and making [antisemitic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-semitic "Anti-semitic"), racist, and [sexist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexist "Sexist") statements.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-indiew-138)[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-141) The film received mixed reviews,[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-142)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-143) and failed at the box office, largely due to this controversy.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-144)[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-145)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-146) In 2011, Foster also appeared as part of an [ensemble cast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ensemble_cast "Ensemble cast") with [John C. Reilly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_C._Reilly "John C. Reilly"), [Kate Winslet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Winslet "Kate Winslet") and [Christoph Waltz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christoph_Waltz "Christoph Waltz") in [Roman Polanski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Polanski "Roman Polanski")'s comedy _[Carnage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnage\_(2011\_film) "Carnage (2011 film)")_, in which the attempts of middle-class parents to settle an incident between their sons descends into chaos. It premiered to mainly positive reviews and earned Foster a Golden Globe nomination as Best Actress.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-RottenTomatoes-147)

## Personal life

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/Jodie_Foster_with_the_LG_Electronics_Kompressor_Vacuum_on_25th_Spirit_Awards_Blue_Carpet_held_at_Nokia_Theatre_L.A._Live_on_March_5%2C_2010_in_LA_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Jodie_Foster_with_the_LG_Electronics_Kompressor_Vacuum_on_25th_Spirit_Awards_Blue_Carpet_held_at_Nokia_Theatre_L.A._Live_on_March_5%2C_2010_in_LA_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jodie_Foster_with_the_LG_Electronics_Kompressor_Vacuum_on_25th_Spirit_Awards_Blue_Carpet_held_at_Nokia_Theatre_L.A._Live_on_March_5,_2010_in_LA_(cropped).jpg)

Foster in 2010

Foster met producer Cydney Bernard, then a production coordinator, on the set of _Sommersby_ (1993).[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-173) They were in a relationship from 1993 until 2008 and had two children together: [Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_B._Foster "Charlie B. Foster") ("Charlie"), born in 1998, and Christopher ("Kit"), born in 2001.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-174) Foster is their biological mother; the biological father's identity has not been made public.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-scotsman-4)[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-vanityfair-175)[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-176)[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-177)[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-178) In 2014, Foster married actress and photographer [Alexandra Hedison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandra_Hedison "Alexandra Hedison") after a year of dating.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-bbched-179)[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-vanityfair-175)

Foster's sexual orientation became the subject of public discussion in 1991 when publications such as _[OutWeek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OutWeek "OutWeek")_ and _[The Village Voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Village\_Voice "The Village Voice"),_ protesting against the alleged homophobia and [transphobia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transphobia "Transphobia") in _The Silence of the Lambs_, claimed she was a lesbian.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollinger2006145%E2%80%93146-180) She publicly acknowledged her 14-year relationship with Bernard in 2007 in a speech at _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_'s "Women in Entertainment" breakfast honoring her.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-observer-12) In 2013, she addressed her decision to [come out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_out "Come out") in a speech after receiving the Cecil B. DeMille Award at the 70th Golden Globe Awards, which led many news outlets to describe her as gay.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-UPI.com-181)[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-APCL-182)[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-ABCNews-183)[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Fischoff-184)[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-bbched-179) Some sources noted that she did not use the words "gay" or "lesbian" in her speech.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Hernandez-2014-05-09-185)

On December 19, 1983, Foster was [detained](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detention_(imprisonment) "Detention (imprisonment)") by U.S. customs agents at [Logan International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logan_International_Airport "Logan International Airport") for possessing a gram of cocaine.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-:0-186)[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-:1-187) She was charged with a [misdemeanor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misdemeanor "Misdemeanor") and placed on one year's probation.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-:2-188)

In 2007, Foster told _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment\_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_ that she is an [atheist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atheism "Atheism"), though she "[loves] religions and the rituals. Even though I don't believe in God, we celebrate pretty much every religion in our family with the kids."[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-189) In 2010, she explained that her family "ritualizes" all holidays: "I take pains to give my family a real religious basis, a knowledge, because it's being well educated. You need to know why all those wars were fought."[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-190) She allowed her children to choose their own religions when they turned 18.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-191)

### John Hinckley Jr. stalking incident

Main article: [Attempted assassination of Ronald Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attempted_assassination_of_Ronald_Reagan "Attempted assassination of Ronald Reagan")

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Jodie_Foster_-_Valley_News_%281981%29.jpg/250px-Jodie_Foster_-_Valley_News_%281981%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jodie_Foster_-_Valley_News_(1981).jpg)

Newspaper clipping, April 2, 1981

During her freshman year at Yale in 1980–81, Foster was stalked by [John Hinckley Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hinckley_Jr. "John Hinckley Jr."), who had developed an obsession with her after watching _Taxi Driver_ multiple times.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Sonneborn-2002-21)(p 74)[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Ewing-McCann-2006-192) He moved to New Haven and tried to contact her by letter and telephone.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Ewing-McCann-2006-192)[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-trial-193) On March 30, 1981, Hinckley [attempted to assassinate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attempted_assassination_of_Ronald_Reagan "Attempted assassination of Ronald Reagan") United States president [Ronald Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan"), wounding him and three other people, claiming that his motive was to impress Foster.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Ewing-McCann-2006-192) The incident drew intense media attention, and Foster was accompanied by bodyguards while on campus.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-rollingstone-7)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Sonneborn-2002-21)(p 74) Judge [Barrington D. Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barrington_D._Parker "Barrington D. Parker") confirmed that Foster was innocent in the case and had been "unwittingly ensnared in a third party's alleged attempt to assassinate an American President". Her videotaped testimony was played at Hinckley's trial.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-observer-12)[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-trial-193) While at Yale, Foster also had other stalkers, including a man who planned to kill her but changed his mind after seeing her perform in a college play.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-rollingstone-7)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-Sonneborn-2002-21)

Foster has seldom publicly commented on Hinckley.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-NYT_1991-10) She wrote an essay, "Why Me?", published in 1982 by _[Esquire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esquire\_(magazine) "Esquire (magazine)")_ on the condition that "there be no cover lines, no publicity and no photos".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-rollingstone-7) In 1991, she canceled an interview on NBC's _[The Today Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Today\_(American\_TV\_program) "Today (American TV program)")_ when she discovered that Hinckley would be mentioned in the introduction and the producers would not change it.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-NYT-1991-10-05-194) She discussed Hinckley in a 1999 interview with [Charlie Rose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Rose "Charlie Rose") on _[60 Minutes II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/60\_Minutes\_II "60 Minutes II")_, explaining that she does not "like to dwell on it too much ... I never wanted to be the actress who was remembered for that event. Because it didn't have anything to do with me. I was kind of a hapless bystander. But ... what a scarring, strange moment in history for me, to be 17 years old, 18 years old, and to be caught up in a drama like that."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-60Minutes-11) She said the incident had a major impact on her career choices, but also acknowledged that her experience was minimal compared to the suffering of Reagan's press secretary, [James Brady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Brady "James Brady"), who was permanently disabled in the shooting and died from his injuries 33 years later, and his loved ones: "Whatever bad moments that I had certainly could never compare to that family."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-60Minutes-11)

## Acting credits and accolades

She also earned the [Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award") in 2013.

*   [49th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/49th_Academy_Awards "49th Academy Awards"), [Best Actress in a Supporting Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress"), nomination, _[Taxi Driver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxi\_Driver "Taxi Driver")_ (1976)

*   [64th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/64th_Academy_Awards "64th Academy Awards"), Best Actress in a Leading Role, _[The Silence of the Lambs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Silence\_of\_the\_Lambs\_(film) "The Silence of the Lambs (film)")_ (1991)
*   [67th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards "67th Academy Awards"), Best Actress in a Leading Role, nomination, _[Nell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nell\_(film) "Nell (film)")_ (1994)
*   [96th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/96th_Academy_Awards "96th Academy Awards"), Best Actress in a Supporting Role, nomination, _[Nyad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyad\_(film) "Nyad (film)")_ (2023)

_[People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People\_(magazine) "People (magazine)")_ magazine named her the most beautiful woman in the world in 1992,[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-195) and in 2003, she was voted Number 23 in [Channel 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_4 "Channel 4")'s countdown of the 100 Greatest Movie Stars of All Time.[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-196)_Entertainment Weekly_ named her 57th on their list of 100 Greatest Movie Stars of All Time in 1996.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-197) In 2016, she was inducted into the [Hollywood Walk of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame "Hollywood Walk of Fame") with a [motion pictures star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_actors_with_Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame_motion_picture_stars "List of actors with Hollywood Walk of Fame motion picture stars") located at 6927 [Hollywood Boulevard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Boulevard "Hollywood Boulevard").[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster#cite_note-198)
